story: On the slow train north, two strangers shared a table and a crossword. Neither of them was any good at it. The older one, a retired surveyor with a pencil behind each ear, insisted that seven down was "gongoozler". The younger one, who had a guitar case and a cold, insisted that no such word existed. They argued through three stations and a tunnel. A conductor stopped to listen and took no side, although he wrote the word on his hand. By the time the hills turned white with frost they had filled in every other square and left that one empty, like a seat saved for someone who might still arrive. At the last stop they shook hands and went their separate ways. Years later, the younger one wrote a song and called it "gongoozler", and never once explained the title to anyone.
